text:
Hydrogen ions (H⁺) are formed when a hydrogen atom loses its electron, most commonly when an acid donates a proton in aqueous solution, where it exists as the hydronium ion (H₃O⁺). The note that hydrogen ions are formed when phosphocreatine breakdown occurs is not the general definition—phosphocreatine breakdown releases energy and involves phosphate transfer, not H⁺ formation as its defining feature.
CONFIDENCE: 90
